scope.baseline: Fresh analysis, ordinary optimized fr CLI, project cache enabled and initially empty per condition/case/repetition. No saved startup or whole-answer store. Same seven questions and explicit limits in every condition.
scope.claims: Disclosed development examples, five repetitions. Unknown startup and exhausted analysis limits must stay unfinished. No unfamiliar-library acceptance, memory saving, ordinary-Python translation overhead or agent-task speedup claim.
scope.phases: Worker base imports, argument parsing, SDK imports and request body have separate internal timers. They exclude some startup and output. Parent startup minus bootstrap is a residual containing interpreter startup, output and scheduling; it is not pure interpreter or SDK cost. Each request starts a new native process for find and dataflow even in a running Python program.
scope.sdk: Same interpreter and SDK source. Source has no SDK bytecode and cannot write it. Installed wheel has checked-hash bytecode compiled before measurement. Both use isolated Python with -I -B; -B still permits reading existing bytecode. Standard-library bytecode and OS file caches remain uncontrolled.
scope.setup: Wheel build, install and checked-hash bytecode compilation have separate recorded one-time costs. They are outside recurring question totals. This is an installed wheel selected by explicit sys.path in the same interpreter, not a virtual-environment activation comparison.
scope.total: Sum of parent process-start-to-ready, each submitted-question-through-parsed-reply interval, and stop-through-process-exit. Includes interpreter startup, imports, arguments, native calls, SDK validation, instrumentation and JSON output. Excludes controller fixture edits, source/bytecode verification and evidence persistence between requests. Wall time also records these controller costs. No uncounted analysis priming.
